speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is going on, can you tell me how long you have had trouble feeding and if you are vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the tenderness on abdominal palpation is concerning. Given the age and symptoms, could you tell me if you have noticed any green (bilious) vomiting or if there has been any passage of stool or gas?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of bilious vomiting, fever, or infection symptoms is noted. Since the baby is 8 months old with a distended, tender abdomen but no passage of stool or gas, have you noticed if he is passing any gas at all, or if his stool has changed in color or consistency?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception.

I need to confirm the stool characteristics immediately. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound.
Please describe the color of any stool passed and tell me if you see or feel any "currant jelly" mucus or blood.
